statements.status_notes: CVE-2010-0928 describes recovering an RSA private key from OpenSSL 0.9.8i on a Gaisler LEON3 processor by injecting faults through a modified supply voltage while it computes a signature, because OpenSSL does not verify the signature before returning it. Exploitation requires physical control over the power supply of the machine doing the signing. OpenSSL disputes the CVE: its maintainers answered on the project's public tracker that the attack needs direct access to the device sufficient to manipulate its voltage and that fault injection is outside OpenSSL's threat model (https://github.com/openssl/openssl/discussions/24540), and OpenSSL's security policy lists physical fault injection among the attack classes it does not treat as vulnerabilities (https://openssl-library.org/policies/general/security-policy/). No upstream fix will ship, and Debian lists no fixed version (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2010-0928). Pending: a maintainer decision on whether that dispute holds for every image built on this package, and a record of that decision in the openssl package README. Until then, an application that must resist fault attacks can verify each signature after creating it.
